title: Mental Health Support Worker
description:
Are you intrested in supporting children's mental health, emotional wellbeing and personal development? Are you looking to gain practical experience within a specialist educational environment while building a career in psychology, mental health, education or therapeutic support?

This Mental Health Support Worker opportunity in Trowbridge, Wiltshire offers meaningful, hands-on experience supporting children with a range of emotional, behavioural and additional needs.

A supportive specialist school in Trowbridge is seeking a compassionate and motivated Mental Health Support Worker to work with children who may have Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC), ADHD, anxiety, emotional regulation difficulties and other additional learning needs.

As a Mental Health Support Worker, you will provide individualised support to help children manage their emotions, develop resilience, build confidence and overcome barriers that may affect their learning and wellbeing.

The Role

As a Mental Health Support Worker, you will provide consistent emotional and pastoral support while helping children develop practical strategies to manage their mental health and everyday challenges.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing 1:1 and small-group support to children with emotional and mental health needs.
- Building positive, trusting relationships with children and becoming a consistent source of support.
- Helping children recognise, communicate and understand their emotions.
- Supporting children to develop emotional regulation and healthy coping strategies.
- Encouraging confidence, self-esteem, resilience and independence.
- Supporting children who may experience anxiety, emotional distress or difficulties managing behaviour.
- Helping children re-engage with learning following periods of emotional or behavioural difficulty.
- Supporting personalised wellbeing, learning and behaviour strategies.
- Promoting positive communication and healthy social interactions.

About You

We are looking for a Mental Health Support Worker who is:
- Compassionate, patient and emotionally resilient.
- Genuinely interested in children's mental health and emotional wellbeing.
- Confident building positive professional relationships with children.
- Calm and consistent when supporting children through challenging emotional situations.
- Understanding of, or willing to learn about, SEMH, Autism, ADHD, anxiety and emotional regulation.
- A strong communicator with excellent listening and relationship-building skills.
- Proactive, reliable and able to adapt their approach to individual children's needs.

Psychology graduates and candidates interested in Educational Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Counselling, Occupational Therapy, Speech and Language Therapy, CAMHS or Teaching are particularly encouraged to apply.

Why Become a Mental Health Support Worker?

This Mental Health Support Worker position provides valuable frontline experience for individuals looking to develop a career within psychology, education, mental health or therapeutic services.

You will gain practical experience in:
- Emotional regulation and wellbeing support.
- Behaviour awareness and positive behaviour strategies.
- Communication and relationship building.
- Supporting children with SEMH and additional needs.
- Safeguarding and professional boundaries.
- Promoting resilience, independence and confidence.
- Working collaboratively with education and specialist professionals.

Working as a Mental Health Support Worker will give you valuable insight into how emotional and mental health can influence children's behaviour, relationships, learning and engagement within education.

What We Offer

This Mental Health Support Worker opportunity provides:
- £85-£110 per day, depending on experience.
- PAYE weekly pay.
- Full-time and part-time opportunities.
- September 2026 start.
- A supportive specialist school environment in Trowbridge, Wiltshire.
- Hands-on experience supporting children with SEMH, Autism, ADHD and additional needs.
- The opportunity to work alongside experienced teachers, therapists and SEN professionals.
- Excellent experience for aspiring psychologists, therapists, educators and mental health professionals.
- The opportunity to develop valuable practical skills while making a genuine difference to children's lives.

Make a Difference as a Mental Health Support Worker

As a Mental Health Support Worker, you will have the opportunity to become a trusted and consistent source of support for children who may find emotional regulation, relationships or learning challenging. Apply today!

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.

title: Autism Support Worker
description:
Autism Support Worker Chippenham, Wiltshire

Chippenham, Wiltshire Full-time & Part-time Available £85-£110 per day September 2026 Start

Are you passionate about supporting autistic children and young people to develop their confidence, independence and communication skills? Do you have an interest in autism, SEND and specialist education and want to gain meaningful experience supporting children with a range of individual needs? This Autism Support Worker opportunity in Chippenham, Wiltshire could be the ideal next step for you.

A specialist school in Chippenham, Wiltshire is seeking a patient, compassionate and dedicated Autism Support Worker to join their team and provide tailored support to children with Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC) and additional needs.

As an Autism Support Worker, you will work closely with children to understand their individual communication styles, sensory needs, interests, strengths and challenges. You will provide consistent, child-centred support that helps children feel safe, understood and able to engage with their education.

The Role

As an Autism Support Worker, your responsibilities will include:
- Providing 1:1 and small-group support to autistic children within the school environment.
- Supporting children with communication, social interaction and emotional regulation.
- Helping children manage sensory needs and supporting them to access appropriate sensory strategies.
- Providing reassurance and guidance during periods of anxiety, distress or dysregulation.
- Supporting children to follow routines and transitions throughout the school day.
- Encouraging independence with learning, communication and everyday activities.
- Supporting positive behaviour through calm, consistent and individualised approaches.
- Helping children develop confidence, self-esteem and social skills.
- Supporting children during classroom activities, break times, lunchtime and other less structured parts of the school day.
- Working alongside specialist teachers and SEN professionals to implement individualised support strategies.

The successful Autism Support Worker will play an important role in creating a calm, structured and inclusive environment where children are encouraged to communicate, participate and develop at their own pace.

About You

We are looking for an Autism Support Worker who is:
- Patient, empathetic and genuinely passionate about supporting autistic children.
- Calm and consistent when responding to children's individual needs.
- Confident building positive and trusting relationships with children.
- Interested in understanding autism, sensory processing, communication and child development.
- Able to adapt their approach to suit different communication and learning styles.
- Observant and able to recognise changes in a child's behaviour, mood or emotional state.
- A strong communicator who can work effectively as part of a wider support team.
- Resilient and able to maintain a positive approach in challenging situations.
- Previous experience supporting autistic children or young people is beneficial but not essential.

Experience as a Teaching Assistant, SEN Teaching Assistant, Support Worker, Care Worker, Youth Worker or Autism Support Worker would be advantageous, although applications are welcomed from graduates and individuals looking to begin a career in specialist education and support.

Why Apply?

This Autism Support Worker position provides valuable hands-on experience supporting autistic children within a specialist educational environment.

The role would be particularly suited to individuals considering future careers in:
- Educational Psychology
- Clinical or Child Psychology
- Speech and Language Therapy
- Occupational Therapy
- Teaching
- Special Educational Needs
- Child Development
- Specialist Support Services

Working as an Autism Support Worker will allow you to develop transferable skills while making a genuine difference to children's educational and personal development.

What We Offer

This Autism Support Worker opportunity provides:
- £85-£110 per day, depending on experience.
- PAYE and weekly pay.
- Full-time and part-time opportunities.
- September 2026 start.
- Hands-on experience supporting autistic children in a specialist setting.
- Exposure to autism-specific strategies and approaches.
- Experience working alongside specialist teachers and SEN professionals.
- Opportunities to develop your understanding of communication, sensory needs, emotional regulation and positive behaviour support.
- Excellent experience for aspiring psychologists, therapists, teachers and SEN professionals.

Start Your Career Supporting Autistic Children

If you are passionate about helping autistic children feel understood, supported and empowered, this Autism Support Worker role in Chippenham could be an excellent opportunity to gain specialist experience.

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.

title: Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker
description:
Are you passionate about supporting children and young people with their emotional wellbeing and mental health? If you're looking to build a rewarding career in psychology, counselling, social work, education, or mental health services, this Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker opportunity in Chippenham, Wiltshire could be the perfect next step.

A welcoming specialist school in Chippenham, Wiltshire is seeking a compassionate and dedicated Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker to support children aged 5-16 with Autism, social, emotional and mental health (SEMH) needs, anxiety, trauma, and additional learning needs. This Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker role offers invaluable experience working alongside experienced teachers, therapists, psychologists, and specialist SEN professionals in a nurturing and therapeutic educational environment.

As an Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker, you will provide one-to-one and small group support to children, helping them develop emotional resilience, confidence, and healthy coping strategies. You will support students in managing their emotions, encourage positive behaviour, build trusting relationships, and help them engage positively in both learning and social activities. The Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker will also work closely with teaching staff to implement wellbeing strategies, promote emotional regulation, and create a safe, structured, and supportive environment where every child can thrive.

This Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker position is ideal for graduates and individuals considering careers in Clinical Psychology, Educational Psychology, Counselling, Social Work, Occupational Therapy, Teaching, or Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS). The experience gained as an Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker will provide an excellent foundation for future study and careers supporting vulnerable children and young people.

Why Apply?
- Gain hands-on experience supporting children with Autism, SEMH, anxiety, trauma, and additional needs.
- Work alongside experienced teachers, therapists, psychologists, and specialist SEN professionals.
- Develop practical skills in emotional regulation, behaviour support, safeguarding, communication, and therapeutic interventions.
- £85-£110 per day.

This Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker opportunity is perfect for someone who is empathetic, patient, and committed to making a lasting difference in the lives of young people. Every day as an Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker will provide opportunities to support pupils through challenges, celebrate their progress, and help them build the confidence and resilience they need to succeed.

If you're looking to gain meaningful experience before progressing into psychology, counselling, education, or mental health, this Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker role in Chippenham, Wiltshire offers the ideal opportunity to develop your skills while making a genuine impact on children's lives.

Apply today for this Emotional and Mental Health Support Worker opportunity in Chippenham, Wiltshire, and begin a rewarding career supporting the emotional wellbeing and mental health of children and young people.
